summary: A concrete lighthouse of 1914 on a Delaware Bay shoal that first held a lightship and the first screw-pile lighthouse in the United States.

structures.note: First screw-pile lighthouse in the US; superstructure removed after 1914, foundation removed about 1963

corrections.why: The 1827 pile tower was destroyed in 1828; the standing tower is the 1914 reinforced-concrete caisson light (NRHP and Commissioner's report). The USLHS record also says cast iron, which the NRHP and Commissioner contradict.
1823 is the lightship; the first lighthouse here lit in 1850 (the 1827 pile tower is the earlier, short-lived tower).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1823 is the lightship, 1827-28 the destroyed pile tower, 1850 the screw-pile lighthouse and 1914 the present concrete tower.

notes_for_editor: Lighthouse Board annual reports for 1850-1895 are not in the local corpus, so the 1850 to 1900 chapters rest on the NRHP nomination, Putnam (1917) and LighthouseFriends (facts only). State: Lighthouse Service reports label the station Delaware; NRHP and record say Cape May County, NJ; NHLPA 2013 also lists it as DE. Appropriation date 11 March (NRHP) vs 4 March 1911 (Commissioner). Caisson: NRHP says finished 14 May 1913, Commissioner says launched 10 July 1913; both give 6 Aug 1913 for placing. First light of 1914: Commissioner 20 Oct, Bulletin announced 22 Oct. 1920 storm line (Bulletin p.9) is a two-column OCR; matched decking sentence to Brandywine by position, please check the page image. 1918 Bulletin rescue OCR is garbled; names matched with roster (Manlove head keeper 1918-1919, Colofen first assistant). Ownership today rests on the NHLPA 2013 list and the Friends' pages; no source read confirms the deed. The Cape May County Herald article on the transfer returned 403. Warrington's 1935 colic story is LighthouseFriends only; the archive lists him as first assistant until 1939, LighthouseFriends calls him keeper. USCG personnel 1961-1970 are listed with names and years only, as the archive prints them. LighthouseFriends names the 1936 and 1923 riprap items not used. Roster lines with person slugs are the archive's own stints.
